requirement:
The generated coverage subchapter MUST make coverage-collection and
post-suite-checking guidance available under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance`, without requiring
separate authored content.
rationale:
The subject requires the generated coverage subchapter to carry coverage-collection and post-suite-checking guidance, as `requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance` describes, with no separately authored content.

The test `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` carries a {test} reference to this requirement. It builds a minimal fixture with no authored coverage chapter. The fixture is a parent chapter, a bare `book.toml` and `SUMMARY.md`, and one source file. It calls `populate_in` and takes the generated `coverage` subchapter. It asserts that the subchapter content contains these strings:
- `habeas test`
- `habeas coverage -- --workspace`
- `habeas coverage-check`
- "after it succeeds,\nrun `habeas coverage-check` as a separate step"
- "`habeas test` collects coverage for the whole workspace,\nthen checks it"
- "static validation test needs no prior coverage"

These map onto the cited guidance obligations:
- Run `habeas coverage-check` as a separate step after `habeas coverage -- --workspace` succeeds.
- Document `habeas test` as collection followed by checking.
- The static validation test needs no prior coverage.

The test also checks other guidance text, such as the 80% target, the `habeas:coverage` citation, and the `habeas author` review. It runs the numbered and unnumbered parent variants. It also asserts that the `:::{coverage-index}` directive is not left in the output, so the content is generated rather than authored.

The guidance comes from the `GUIDANCE` constant in `src/execution_coverage.rs`, whose text matches these assertions.

The test does not assert the "CI step" wording. It also does not assert the "successful full-workspace instrumented nextest run" wording separately. The "after it succeeds" assertion covers the sequencing, so this is not a material gap. The "bundled agent instructions" half of `check.guidance` is not part of this subject, which concerns the generated subchapter.

I found no gap and no {fixme} acknowledgments apply.
